label: Naming God inside a modal context: descriptive versus reference-fixed
term: naming God inside a modal context
resolution: The stage-one naming premises (STMT-GOD-NAMES-THE-UNIQUE-MAXIME-ENS, STMT-GOD-NAMES-THE-FULLY-DESCRIBED-PRINCIPLE, STMT-MAXIME-ENS-IS-GOD) evaluate the name in one model with no worlds; at the reference world the two senses designate the same bearers (GodNamingSenses Laws, clause 2), so those premises are neutral between them. The senses diverge only when 'God' occurs under a box, as in the necessary-being node STMT-NECESSARY-ROOT-BOX-K, where the world-invariant GOD_4 predicate is applied to one fixed root n and n's existence is boxed. That node is logically equivalent to its GOD_NAMING_2 reading (NecessaryRootRigidName, theorem rigidIffBoxK). Its GOD_NAMING_1 reading (NecessaryRootDescriptiveName) is a different proposition: neither entails the other (Separation controls); the descriptive reading gives the box node with the open bridge NoOtherPossibleGod, and the box node gives the descriptive reading with GodhoodEssentialToGod and NoOtherPossibleGod. A third reading, a name whose sense is the description, has the world-intension of GOD_NAMING_1 under narrow scope and of GOD_NAMING_2 under wide scope; it is not a separate sense here. Each argument uses one sense; the premise-free controls comparing both are marked as sense-mixing controls.
